item.title: Reigando Cave: Musashi Miyamoto's Retreat — Guide
item.description: Reigando, a mountain cave in the hills west of Kumamoto city, is famous as the retreat where the legendary swordsman and philosopher Miyamoto Musashi spent his final years and wrote his celebrated treatise on strategy and swordsmanship, ‘The Book of Five Rings’ (Go Rin no Sho), around 1643. Undefeated in over sixty duels, Musashi withdrew to this quiet cave to meditate and set down his life’s wisdom, and the atmospheric grotto — with a small shrine and statue inside — has drawn pilgrims and admirers ever since.

item.title: Takachiho's Sacred Caves — Guide
item.description: The Takachiho area is home to sacred caves at the very heart of Japan’s foundational creation mythology, making them among the most spiritually charged natural sites in the country. The most famous is linked to the legend of Amaterasu, the sun goddess, who — angered by her brother — hid herself in a heavenly rock cave (Ama-no-Iwato), plunging the world into darkness until the other gods gathered to lure her out.
